By Brittany Carter

Topic:Netball

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 1:53pm

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 11:47pm

Thunderbirds players celebrate their semifinal win. (Getty: Sarah Reed)

The Adelaide Thunderbirds are the first team to secure a spot in the 2026 Super Netball grand final with a win over the Melbourne Vixens 58-44 in the major semi at the Adelaide 36ers Arena.

They will now have a week off as they wait to find out who the opponent that stands in their way of a third trophy in four years will be, having clinched back-to-back titles already in 2023 and 2024.

The Vixens will host the West Coast Fever in the preliminary final on Saturday June 27 at John Cain Arena, after the latter defeated the Melbourne Mavericks 56-52 in the minor semi, knocking them out of the race.

Sunday's matches had similar themes. Both saw experienced coaches outwit rookie coaches. Both had momentum turn in the second quarter. Both were a lesson in self-belief.

The Thunderbirds lost the opening stanza of their game 14-12. They were flat in defence and took a moment to adapt to the relentless pressure from the Vixens.

Tania Obst knows her team inside and out. (Getty: Sarah Reed)

Addressing the lack of energy, coach Tania Obst moved Latanya Wilson into GD to partner fellow Jamaican Shamera Sterling-Humphrey at GK. These two thrive together and have similar game styles with incredible closing speed and the aerial ability to fly high for loose ball. Typically Obst turns to these combinations late in a game, but here she sensed they needed it earlier. With that change in the second quarter the back line of the Thunderbirds came alive.

At the opposite end of the court, Vixens defensive duo Jo Weston and Kate Eddy were given the bold nod by coach Di Honey to start the game. Honey had already trialled this back in round six against the Thunderbirds and it had been quite effective. So she kept the surprise move in her back pocket for finals.

In the beginning, Weston and Eddy had the Thunderbirds' measure. They tag teamed goal shooter Elmeré van der Berg and shut down the tall target under the post. They restricted her ability to present to the feeders, meaning the competition's leading goal scorer managed just 10 goals in both the first and second quarters.

But as the Thunderbirds' confidence grew at the back of the court, it filtered its way down to the attackers. The ball was coming back twice as fast in transition and Van der Berg started to find her groove. Down 25-23 at half-time, the Vixens coach decided it was time to mix it up and resort to more obvious defence options, such as an Emily Mannix or Rudi Ellis in GK with Jo Weston in GD. The retreat to the obvious only opened up the game further for Van Der Berg, who went on to pile 31 more goals in the final half on her way to the Player of the Match award. During the final 30 minutes, she went on two four-goal scoring streaks and a five-goal streak as well.

Elmeré van der Berg is the player of the match in the major semifinal. (Getty: Sarah Reed)

Yet, Honey never turned back to the Eddy and Weston combo. Why? The changes made in this game felt reactive. Maybe there's something in that. Has Honey worked out how to get the best out of her players and the team in general yet? Do they need to be left out there to figure it out?

It doesn't help that the Vixens drop their heads when they're down. That's something they've unfortunately made a habit of in the back half of the season, losing four of their five past games.

They had to rely on two-point super shots to keep the score within touching distance. Kiera Austin and Lily Graham together tallied seven. In comparison, the Thunderbirds had none. They didn't even need to attempt them until the final quarter when the game was in the bag.

"It was a real arm wrestle there in the first half," Obst said.

"Our ability to mix things up, we've made quite deliberate changes throughout the season and there's no doubt that when we did make some of those changes today that they had affect."

There were similar themes in the Fever and Mavericks semifinal, as the home side pulled off a nine-goal turnaround in the second period and went toe-to-toe in a grinding affair.

Coach Dan Ryan wanted to reward Zoe Cransberg for her game-winning intercept in round 14, and so once again gave her the start at centre. When it became clear that she was probably too inexperienced for that role and a bit overwhelmed by the occasion, he swapped Zoe with her twin sister.

Jordan Cransberg started last year's grand final for the Fever in centre and was ready to go when she came off the bench as a super sub in the second quarter. In the remaining 45 minutes on court against a tough opposing player of the calibre of Aussie Diamond Jamie Lee-Price, Cransberg only had one turnover. She was a more sure option in the middle and accurate on the feed, finishing with nine goal assists.

"She came into the game in a very tough situation, down at quarter time ... I thought her ability to back herself, see the space and let the ball go at the right time was killer today, she was errorless in quarter two and quarter three, it was brilliant in a pressurised situation," Ryan said.

"It really was a catalyst for us growing our momentum and confidence in our front line."

Dan Ryan knew the changes he needed to make to get his team firing. (Getty: James Worsfold)

The other key change from Ryan was to bring on Ruth Aryang at goal keeper. The 22-year-old is still trying to find where she fits in this line-up after being sidelined for most of 2025 with an Achilles injury, but Ryan has eventually unlocked her strengths. Alternating her with Jamaican Kadie-Ann Dehaney as the last line of defence four times from that second quarter onwards, the pair kept the Mavericks guessing. Aryang was full of energy chasing after ball. In 32 minutes of game time, the super sub topped the gains stat for her team (four). Dehaney was more of a physical presence owning the space.

"Ruth looked like she had an absolute ball out there, she offered a great little impact change for us in the goal keeper position ... she and [Dehaney] play it very differently and just her confidence to back herself and go after the contest, she came up with some critical stuff," Ryan said.

"We wanted to make sure that we kept challenging Mavericks' level of comfort in the lines they were running and their playing style ... both of them were seamless, it's not an easy job to do to come on and come off ... I think it's a great weapon that we've unearthed late in the season."

Where we'd argue the Fever won this match tactically, was their reliance on experience and the element of surprise. The Mavericks shooters weren't able to adjust with so much rotation in the GK bib. It's also important to note that not a single one of the Mavericks players have won a grand final.

Ruth Aryang looks to block a shot by Uneeq Palavi at Perth Arena. (Getty: Paul Kane)

The Fever have a core group of players that have been there and done that. Jess Anstiss, Alice Teague-Neeld and Sasha Glasgow were all apart of the Fever's 2022 premiership tilt. Romelda Aiken-George and Dehaney have won premierships with other clubs. They're used to the big stage, they just mentally needed to lock in, and Ryan turned to them in the dying moments to pull the side through. All five of these experienced athletes were on court for the final whistle.

Last week, the team needed to win by at least eight goals to secure a home semifinal. They won by nine. That built a huge amount of confidence and self-belief.

Whereas judging by the Mavericks' temperament in their final timeout, it looked like they'd already resigned themselves to a loss. Why they didn't do the same and turn to an experienced Shimona Nelson in her ninth Super Netball campaign was also confusing. She finished with 100 per cent accuracy and 33 goals, watching the fourth quarter from the bench. Although it hurts now, the Mavericks players and coaching staff will learn a lot from their first ever finals campaign.

"The fact that this was the Mavericks' first final, we knew they would be up and about, but that we have experience in these moments ... and knowing it's a different [mental] game come finals," Fever captain Anstiss said.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:56pm

By Brittany Carter

Thanks for tuning into ABC Sport's live coverage of the Super Netball semifinals. What a cracking day! We'll have more analysis for you at the top of the page in due course, but we'll wrap the blog here.

Thunderbirds through to the Grand Final.

Vixens and Fever set to contest the Preliminary Final.

Mavericks knocked out of the race.

Key Event

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:56pm

By Brittany Carter

It's clear the penalty count went against the Mavericks here. A big difference between their final count and the Fever's. That's honestly the only real difference here, the gains, time in possession and turnovers are all pretty even. So those 16 extra penalties were costly for the visitors.

The centre pass and goal to gain success rate indicates the Fever were slightly better with ball in hand. Mavericks wasted their defensive wins, there was a lot of long passing that played right into the hands of the Fever. They had a maximum five goal lead in the first quarter and were uable to keep that stammina up throughout the full 60 minutes as the Fever came roaring home like a freight train. Finals experience was a key factor too. Would the result have been different with a more experienced goal attack on court for the Mavs and Shimona Nelson in GS? Both the Mavs players and coaches will learn a lot from this game.

Key Event

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:43pm

By Brittany Carter

The Fever wing attack can barely hear the host broadcaster in her player of the match interview, the 12,332-strong crowd is so loud in Perth. After 60 minutes on court, she finishes the game with a whopping 45 feeds, 29 goal assists, 15 centre pass receives, three pickups.

Key Event

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:40pm

By Brittany Carter

The Fever are through to the preliminary final!

An insane final couple of minutes saw both teams throw the ball away, some insane bits of defence. A few missed attempts at the super shot from the Mavs and two clutch rebounds from Fever goal keeper Kadie-Ann Dehaney to see out the game.

"SETTLE!" was yelled on both occasions by Glasgow and Dehaney at the end. The Mavericks are in tears, they threw everything at it but unfortunately some of the tactics and execution were off at the end there. They relied on a very young moving circle to try and get them back in front with the high-risk, high-reward super shot. But in finals like this a tall holding shooter like Aiken-George is always going to be the steady and safe option. She was a key difference at the death.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:35pm

By Brittany Carter

McDonald gets a super shot to bring the game within three goals and just two minutes left in the minor semifinal. THIS IS TENSE!

SCORE: Fever lead 55-52

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:34pm

By Brittany Carter

A crucial intercept from Mavs captain Amy Parmenter has sparked some energy for her side. They convert the opportunity. While a Uneeq Palavi super shothas got them a crucial two points back on the scoreboard.

SCORE: Fever lead 55-50

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:31pm

By Brittany Carter

Mavericks coach Gerard Murphy has called a timeout with 4:48 on the clock as the game has entered its final super shot period. It was very calm and level headed. If this was another team like the Vixens it would be all about the rev up and we can still win this. Instead it was a very casual approach to chatting tactics.

"How are we going to get the ball into the super shot?"

"Come on, let's go have some fun this last bit."

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:28pm

By Brittany Carter

The Mavericks have seriously slipped in standards in this final quarter and the game is starting to get away from them as the Fever smell a home win. A 10-goal scoreline can be brought back with the super shot, but the Mavs have also got their youngest stars out on court. Can they deliver in a big-time game? There's a reason most coaches look to experience in these moments.

SCORE: Fever lead 54-44

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:26pm

By Brittany Carter

My goodness, Ruth Aryang is having a field day. In her first season back from an achilles injury, she is relishing the opportunity to be out on court in a finals game. Her impact is clearly rattling the Mavericks too, as McDonald is called for an offensive contact while trying to get away from Aryang and gifts the ball to the Fever.

SCORE: Fever lead 53-43

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:19pm

By Brittany Carter

Uneeq Palavi has been given the nod by coach Gerard Murphy to start this fourth and final quarter. Palavi was named in the Tonga Tala Commonwealth Games team this week. With her team down by four, she is known for her super shot distance and playing with a lot of flair. Palavi has also combined with McDonald in the shooting circle at the end of several succesful Mavericks games. Once again they turn to their younger shooting combo. Will it work this game?

Key Event

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:14pm

By Brittany Carter

Mavericks waste a chance to score one more goal before the final break of the game, completely spraying the ball out of court. Fever jump on the opportunity and Glasgow slots another goal for them right on the whistle. The Fever have won both of the middle quarters now. There were four lead changes in that third quarter. How crazy! This game is a grind and they're in it for the long haul.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:12pm

By Brittany Carter

The English captain Fran Williams spotted that from a mile away. Flying backwards against the flight off the ball she intercepts a ball meant for Maddie Hay.

SCORE: Fever lead 43-40

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:11pm

By Brittany Carter

The Fever had the ball in hand close to the post and with the lead, they didn't necessarily need to go after the super shot. But Romelda Aiken-George passed back to the edge of the circle looking to set up in the two-point zone and it was fumbled by Alice Teague-Neeld.

SCORE: Fever lead 41-39

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:07pm

By Brittany Carter

Taking a ball mid-air and sailing into the circle she lands on the foot of the new GK on court Charlotte Sexton. It clearly hurt and Glasgow ends up on the ground grabbing at her leg, but it wasn't intentional. Good news is Glasgow looks happy to continue. She suffered a horrific leg break a couple of years ago when she was playing at the Mavericks, so it's always a bit worrying when she goes down.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:04pm

By Brittany Carter

Nelson collected a pass but was off balance after a challenge from Aryang. She fell backwards and lost the ball and next thing you know the Fever pick it up, run off with it and manage to get back in front. This score keeps too-ing and fro-ing. Mavericks head coach Gerard Murphy calls a tactical timeout and speaks with his midcourters, asking them to refine their approach to the feed into the circle. Then to Nelson, addressing her fall on court he said:

"Don't worry about that, shit happens."

He always seem to be pretty chilled in his approach. Nice to know that doesn't change in finals. Coming out of that break in play, Sacha McDonald enters the game at GA replacing Batcheldor.

SCORE: Fever lead 35-33

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:01pm

By Brittany Carter

Intercepts from Jessie Grenvold and Amy Parmenter see the Mavericks get themselves back in front. It feels like the desperate, relentless efforts of these two players may pull the Mavericks through the tougher moments of this semifinal. Both of them named in the Aussie Diamonds squad for 2026/27 and with good reason.

SCORE: Mavs lead 33-31

Key Event

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 4:49pm

By Brittany Carter

The Mavericks are on the wrong end of the penalty count here. Six extra penalties. They do lead the gain stat though, so they're in the contest. It's just whether that'll come back to bite them as the game goes on. Not much else to comment on here.

The Mavericks gain to goal rate is excellent. Sitting at 100 per cent they are rewarding their defenders and making sure they turn their efforts to win ball into goals. They do need to up their execution in attack though, there's barely anything in the game but the Fever have been slightly more accurate on that front. With an extremely tall holding shooter, they can score quickly. So as the opposition you've got to make sure you match them in that area and convert your own centre pass.

Key Event

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 4:44pm

By Brittany Carter

A nine-goal turnaround for the Fever in that quarter felt like it came out of nowhere. The injections of 22-year-old defender Ruth Aryang into GK midway through the quarter has lit a fire in the home side. With fresh legs and a hit of energy, Aryang has been getting a touch on everything and keeping Mavericks goal shooter Shimona Nelson on her toes. Nelson looked really comfortable to start the game, so it was important they found a way to stem her flow of goals. The Cransberg swap in the middle also had immediate impact. Jordan Cransberg has been safer with ball in hand at C.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 4:39pm

By Brittany Carter

It's a super shot off. Sasha Glasgow says anything you can do, I can do too. She levels the score.

SCORE: 27-all

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 4:38pm

By Brittany Carter

The Mavericks shoot looonggg. And score a two-point goal from the wide arc.

SCORE: Mavs lead 27-25
